subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification — call recap & numbers
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-14T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification — call recap & next steps

Ava / team — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our call and a few clarifying questions so we can put together a ballpark quote: 

1) Expected production token volumes (please confirm): you mentioned ~30M tokens/day baseline, with weekday peaks up to ~100M tokens/day and monthly batch/analytics spikes ~200M tokens/day. Is that the correct baseline/peak/analytics split?

2) Workload shape & model: you said the main real-time workload is a fine-tuned Llama-2-70B variant used for customer-facing recommendations (avg ~40 tokens per request). Offline batch embedding/rerank jobs will also run overnight.

3) Throughput/latency targets: you mentioned p50 latency target ~200ms, p95 under 500ms for single-turn chat. For throughput you called out a steady-state of ~1k tokens/sec with burst capacity up to ~5k tokens/sec. Confirm?

4) GPU preference and ops: you said you'd prefer H100 80GB nodes but are open to A100 if it materially improves cost. Initial ask is a reserved pool of 4 GPUs with option to scale to ~12 over the next 3 months.

5) Budget / unit economics: can you confirm an internal target $/1M tokens range? On the call you suggested the budget is in the $40k-$60k/month neighborhood for committed capacity. Does that still hold?

Next steps: if you can confirm the items above I'll put together a conservative dedicated capacity ballpark (reserved GPU monthly, expected throughput coverage, and an estimated $/1M tokens given caching/batching effects). I've attached the short pricing/template worksheet to make the numbers explicit — feel free to drop the token profile CSV if helpful.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing-template.xlsx (worksheet stub)

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Ava Reynolds <ava@finlytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: 2028-02-14T11:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification — call recap & next steps

Hi Dylan — thanks for the recap. Confirming the numbers from our side: 

- Production baseline: ~30M tokens/day (averaged across weekday traffic).
- Production peak: up to ~100M tokens/day during high activity windows.
- Offline batch/analytics: additional ~200M tokens/day during nightly jobs (not latency sensitive).
- Model: Llama-2-70B fine-tuned; typical response 30-50 tokens; embeddings pipeline uses the same base model for reranking.
- Throughput/latency: target p50 ~180-220ms, p95 <= 500ms for production traffic. Steady throughput target ~1,000 tokens/sec, and we need burst headroom to ~5,000 tokens/sec for marketing events.
- GPU preference: H100 80GB preferred for performance; open to A100 if the price delta is meaningful.
- Reserved capacity: initial commit = 4 GPUs, need ability to add up to 12 within 8-12 weeks.
- Budget: our procurement target for committed capacity + license is $45k–$55k/month.
- Target unit economics: we're aiming for ~$20–30 per 1M tokens for production (post-batching/caching).

I've attached a token profile CSV with hourly token distribution and sample request sizes. Let us know if you need more granularity.

Thanks,
Ava Reynolds
Head of ML Platforms | Finlytics
Attachment: Finlytics_token_profile.csv (CSV stub)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-14T12:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification — Finlytics (ballpark ask)

Marissa / Marcus — forwarding Finlytics confirmation above. Key asks they want covered in our ballpark: 
- Initial reserved pool: 4 x H100(80GB) (scale target to 12)
- Workload: steady 1k tokens/sec, burst 5k tokens/sec; p95 latency <= 500ms; model = Llama-2-70B-finetuned
- Monthly budget target: $45k–$55k for reserved capacity + license. Target unit economics from buyer: $20–$30 / 1M tokens.

Can you: 
1) Provide a conservative monthly reserved pricing for 4 x H100 incl. standard support + 99.9% uptime SLA and an uplift for autoscale/burst?
2) Quick calc for expected $/1M tokens given their steady/burst mix (accounting for caching/batching assumptions) — give low/likely/high per 1M token bands.
3) Any recommended deployment pattern (e.g., 3 active + 1 standby, or all active with autoscale) that balances cost vs headroom?

I'll stitch the answers into a short email back to Ava with a suggested next step (canary pilot + 30-day credit for performance verification).

Thanks,
Dylan
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-15T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification — ballpark and next steps

Ava — appreciate the confirm. Per internal sizing and a quick cost model, here's a conservative ballpark to help procurement: 

Ballpark (monthly, committed):
- Reserved 4 x H100 (80GB) pool: $42,000/month (includes standard enterprise support and 99.9% uptime SLA).
- Autoscale/burst buffer add-on (on-demand GPUs for spikes up to 12 total): billed at usage rates; assume ~20% uplift on months with major events.

Estimated unit economics (production traffic, after caching & batching):
- Low (aggressive batching + prefix caching): ~$15 / 1M tokens
- Likely (expected mix they described): ~$22 / 1M tokens
- High (minimal caching, heavy real-time inference): ~$35 / 1M tokens

Notes / assumptions:
- Numbers assume the Llama-2-70B variant runs efficiently on H100 80GB and that we can leverage KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts and batched offline jobs.
- Offline batch tokens are charged at a lower per-token rate in our model (we can reflect that in a formal proposal).
- We recommend starting with a 3 active + 1 standby pattern for the 4-GPU pool to keep p95 latency headroom while reducing single-GPU overcommit risk. This gives predictable latency and straightforward autoscale to add more GPUs for bursts.

Recommended next steps:
1) We can run a 30-day canary on 2 GPUs (trial credits applied) to validate throughput & p95 latency with your payload.
2) If results look good, roll to 4 reserved GPUs and sign a 12-month committed plan for better unit economics.
3) Procurement: I'll share a formal quote + SOW that splits production vs batch pricing and includes add-on autoscale options.

Would you like a short 30-minute call early next week to review the canary plan and timelines?

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-ballpark-quote.pdf (stub)

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
